description: Audit the project's Python and npm dependencies for known security vulnerabilities and outdated packages. It reads the dependency files in the workspace (requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Pipfile.lock, package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json), checks every pinned package against the OSV.dev vulnerability database, and looks up the latest release of the direct dependencies on PyPI and npm. Use it when the user asks whether their dependencies are safe or up to date, before shipping or deploying, or after writing or changing a requirements or lock file. Turn the result into a short answer: lead with the critical and high vulnerabilities and the upgrade that fixes each, then the rest briefly, then the most important outdated packages (warn that major updates can break things). Only quote advisories, versions and links the tool returned. Don't edit dependency files unless the user asks; when they do, change only the versions the report names and run the project's tests afterwards. Requirements without an exact version can't be checked; the report lists them, and auditing the lock file instead covers them. Its output ends with [chart] lines, which the chat draws as charts for the user (vulnerabilities by severity, and the dependencies checked by how far behind): don't repeat those numbers or redraw them with generate_chart unless the user asks for an image file. With export=true it also writes dep_audit/findings.json to the workspace.
author: Hannes Hapke

path.description: A dependency file or a folder, relative to /workspace. Defaults to the whole workspace (folders up to four levels deep; node_modules, virtualenvs and build output are skipped).

include_dev.description: Also check development and test dependencies.

check_latest.description: Also look up the latest release of each direct dependency (at most 80).

export.description: Also write every finding as JSON to dep_audit/findings.json in the workspace.
